problem: Concurrent agents could mutate one candidate while CI was running, causing head thrash, restarted workflows, main drift and apparent chat stalls.
root_cause: Concurrency admission happened mainly after mutation instead of predictively before mutation.
Remote workflow waiting behaved too synchronously.
System Map writeback could wake unrelated platform suites.
Stale production snapshots could queue behind newer main.
The post-merge obligation terminalizer unconditionally waited for a Netlify website release even when a merged obligation changed only governance and delivery-control-plane files.
prevention: Exactly one active writer per obligation.
Build non-conflicting obligations in parallel; serialize only terminal overlap.
Checkpoint before remote wait and continue independent work.
Supersede stale reversible production snapshot work.
Do not wake Business OS or portal native tests for System Map-only writeback.
For governance-only/control-plane merges, terminal production proof is current-main containment; do not poll Netlify for a deployment that is not applicable.
Scope the scheduler config itself to the automation lane so governance tuning cannot fan out into portal or website release lanes.
